item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-57f7178185cc827b","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"On 30 August 2023 in Goma, security forces confronted a banned Wazalendo-linked protest against MONUSCO and other international organizations; a local civil-society official reported 26 civilians killed and at least 50 injured, while the army said protesters killed a policeman, fired live rounds, and arrested 160 people.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the security-force response to Congolese authorities under President Félix Tshisekedi, but does not establish his personal order for the operation.","limitations":["Casualty figures and accounts were preliminary and contested.","The source does not report prosecutions, disciplinary action, or presidential review."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6badec2ed9ed8b1b","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"UNFPA reported that approximately 220,000 women were pregnant in eastern DRC and 55,000 were expected to give birth within three months; healthcare infrastructure was fragile and access to maternal and newborn services was exceptionally difficult.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"August 2023","ruler_attribution":"The finding describes conditions during Tshisekedi's presidency but does not attribute the service-access deficit to a specific presidential decision.","limitations":["The report focuses on Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu and does not isolate government versus donor or humanitarian responsibility.","It provides no national counterfactual or year-on-year outcome estimate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6badec2ed9ed8b1b","start_unit":9,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"UNFPA reported a significant increase in sexual violence in eastern DRC during 2023; displaced women and girls faced heightened rape and assault risks, survival sex was reported in camps, and access to medical, psychosocial, legal, and socioeconomic support was limited.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.10","6B.3","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"The report documents conditions under the national authorities led by Tshisekedi but does not identify a specific presidential policy as their cause.","limitations":["The report is humanitarian and regional rather than a formal attribution of state responsibility.","It records reported conditions and service limitations, not a complete incidence estimate."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f69b31756f715a9f","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The CENCO-ECC election-observation mission reported that corruption affected the 2023 electoral process, including vote buying in senatorial and provincial-governor elections; illegal detention of electoral materials, fraud, destruction, and physical attacks on CENI staff; and corruption suspicions involving some judges handling electoral disputes.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.5","4B.10","7B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the electoral institutions and political environment during Tshisekedi's administration; the source does not prove that Tshisekedi personally directed the reported corruption.","limitations":["The article summarizes an observer mission's findings and recommendations rather than adjudicated findings against the president.","The report recommends investigations and sanctions, indicating that accountability outcomes were not established in the supplied units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-843c9fb98aa45cd5","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"After a security meeting concerning fighting around Kitshanga and North Kivu, Tshisekedi's government stated that measures were being taken to block Rwanda and M23 and appealed again to the international community over the population's suffering.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.3","2B.9","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"January 2023","ruler_attribution":"The account reports Tshisekedi's security meeting and the government's public position through the communications minister.","limitations":["The source records stated intentions and diplomatic appeals, not the measures' implementation or effectiveness.","The attribution of Rwandan involvement is presented as the government's claim."]},{"source_id":"SRC-843c9fb98aa45cd5","start_unit":6,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi directed government and social actors to address children living in the street and called for a national child-protection strategy, concrete and durable reintegration measures, and government and partner support for family, social, and economic reintegration.","question_ids":["6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"January 2023","ruler_attribution":"The policy direction was issued by Tshisekedi through the Council of Ministers and reported by the government spokesperson.","limitations":["The source does not document funding, implementation, coverage, or outcomes during 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1c8777ca0523555a","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, Tshisekedi announced a gradual easing of the state of siege in North Kivu and Ituri, including ending a curfew and allowing peaceful demonstrations and more normal civilian life; the state of siege had transferred authority from civilian institutions to the military and police since 2021.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"October 2023","ruler_attribution":"The announcement and stated resolution were made personally by Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The announcement was gradual and the supplied report does not establish full implementation by year-end.","Amnesty International reported that military authorities had undermined expression, assembly, and access to justice with impunity, while violence continued."]},{"source_id":"SRC-36a1233129f714c1","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"On 18 January 2023 in Goma, police fired tear gas at an unauthorized protest against the arrival of foreign troops; authorities detained some protesters and journalists covering the demonstration.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"January 2023","ruler_attribution":"The response was carried out by police under the national government led by Tshisekedi; the source does not establish a personal presidential order.","limitations":["The source does not report the number of detainees, legal grounds, injuries, or subsequent remedies.","Authorities stated that the protest was unauthorized."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6f88fbf367767b21","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In April 2023, Tshisekedi announced a plan to pre-canton and disarm M23 elements at Kitshanga, transfer them to a site near Kindu, and prepare them for integration into the PDDRCS; he also said he had observed delays in M23 withdrawal and supported the regional diplomatic process.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"April 2023","ruler_attribution":"The plan and assessment of delays were stated personally by Tshisekedi at a press conference.","limitations":["The source reports an announced plan, not completed cantonment, disarmament, integration, or durable peace outcomes.","Tshisekedi simultaneously described M23 as manipulated by Rwanda and said negotiations with terrorists were excluded, limiting evidence of a comprehensive settlement approach."]},{"source_id":"SRC-dccee679d7d1f405","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi's PDL-145T was presented as a nationally funded program to reduce rural-urban and territorial inequalities through health centers, primary schools, and administrative buildings; three implementing agencies were expected to begin delivering infrastructure in July 2023, with planned financing of $300 million for 2021, $700 million for 2022, and $660.1 million for 2023, totaling about $1.66 billion.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"June-July 2023","ruler_attribution":"The program was initiated by Tshisekedi and the delivery timetable and financing were presented by him and his government.","limitations":["The article reports planned funding and announced delivery, not verified execution, quality, distribution, or completed outcomes.","The financing schedule begins in 2021 and therefore is not wholly attributable to 2023 decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-0cbb00418e0622a6","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In January 2023, Tshisekedi's Presidential Council for Strategic Monitoring adopted a 2023 roadmap to track presidential commitments; the council reported primary-education fee abolition as fulfilled, while universal health coverage and free maternity care remained in implementation and faced difficulties.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.5","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"January 2023","ruler_attribution":"The council was chaired and created by Tshisekedi, and its coordinator reported on progress against his commitments.","limitations":["The claims of fulfillment and progress come from the president's monitoring body and are not independently evaluated in the supplied article.","The source acknowledges implementation difficulties but does not quantify service coverage or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b0bc45cbd86a7a48","start_unit":11,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"UNESCO described its DRC Spotlight Study as a national education-system diagnosis based on evidence, examining progress and constraints across educational vision, teaching and learning, teachers, administration and management, community engagement, and assessment of foundational education.","question_ids":["6B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"2023 context","ruler_attribution":"The study concerns the DRC education system during Tshisekedi's period but does not attribute its findings or recommendations to him personally.","limitations":["The supplied page provides the study's purpose but not its substantive findings, indicators, or recommendations.","No concrete 2023 policy outcome is reported in the supplied units."]},{"source_id":"SRC-63e312e6a5627df6","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In May 2023, Tshisekedi publicly accused the opposition of trying to create tensions that would prevent elections and insisted elections would occur on the constitutional timetable; opposition figures protesting near CENI were prevented from reaching its headquarters by police, while the electoral process and CENI were contested by opposition parties.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.10","7B.1","7B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"May 2023","ruler_attribution":"The accusations and commitment to hold elections were made personally by Tshisekedi; the police response occurred under his government.","limitations":["The article reports competing political claims and does not independently determine whether the opposition intended to disrupt elections or whether CENI was reliable.","The source does not establish whether Tshisekedi personally ordered the police perimeter or whether later remedies occurred."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b97de01043631a87","start_unit":5,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"On 8 July 2023, Tshisekedi appointed or reconfirmed managers and board chairs across numerous public enterprises and regulatory bodies, including institutions for entrepreneurship, statistics, agriculture, transport, public employment, strategic minerals, victim reparations, disaster management, and state airlines and railways.","question_ids":["4B.5","5B.2","5B.6","6B.4","7B.5","8B.4"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"July 2023","ruler_attribution":"The appointments were made by presidential ordinances and announced through the public broadcaster.","limitations":["The source lists appointments but provides no selection criteria, qualifications, performance record, political ties, or subsequent institutional results.","The breadth of appointments does not by itself establish either professionalization or patronage."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains nine documents, including several reports of planned measures or institutional conditions without verified implementation or outcome evidence.","Attribution to Tshisekedi is direct for his statements, presidential appointments, and chaired presidential monitoring, but often indirect for police or military conduct and humanitarian conditions.","No source supplied concrete evidence relevant to nuclear, biological, AI, or other catastrophic-risk governance lenses beyond the absence of such material in the documents."]}
